subject: Applied Mechanics & Design
summary: a rapid formula revision of Engineering Mechanics (SHM, moments of inertia, power on a gradient), Strength of Materials (section modulus, Mohr's circle, shear-stress distribution), Theory of Machines (gear trains with idlers, Coriolis acceleration, secondary unbalanced force), Vibrations (damped natural frequency, torsional vibration, springs in series and parallel) and Machine Design (bolt tightening torque, V-belt tensions, Wahl factor) — every solution states the key formula, so the set doubles as a revision sheet

questions.text: A particle moves in simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 50 mm. Its maximum speed is 0.5 m/s. Its maximum acceleration is
solution: Concept: In SHM x = A sin ωt, so vmax = Aω and amax = Aω² = vmax²/A; period T = 2π/ω.
ω = v<sub>max</sub>/A = 0.5/0.05 = 10 rad/s.
amax = Aω² = 0.05 × 10² = 5 m/s² (C). (Period = 2π/10 = 0.628 s.)
Exam tip: Velocity is maximum at the mean position and acceleration at the extremes; 10 m/s² comes from forgetting the amplitude (using ω² × 0.1).

questions.text: A thin uniform circular disc has a mass of 4 kg and a radius of 0.2 m. Its mass moment of inertia about a tangent lying in the plane of the disc is
solution: Concept: Disc: Ipolar = ½mr²; Idiameter = ¼mr² (perpendicular-axis theorem); then the parallel-axis theorem I = IG + md².
Tangent in the plane is parallel to a diameter at distance r: I = ¼mr² + mr² = (5/4)mr².
Exam tip: Tangent perpendicular to the plane gives (3/2)mr² = 0.24 kg·m² — read which tangent is meant. Ring values: mr², ½mr², (3/2)mr², 2mr².

questions.text: A car of mass 1200 kg climbs a road of gradient 1 in 20 (measured along the slope) at a steady 54 km/h. The road and air resistance together is 300 N. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the power developed by the engine, in kW, is ______
solution: Concept: Power = tractive force × speed; at steady speed the tractive force = mg sinθ + resistance.
1 in 20 along the slope means sinθ = 1/20: mg sinθ = 1200 × 9.81/20 = 588.6 N.
Exam tip: Convert km/h to m/s (÷ 3.6) before multiplying. On an accelerating car add ma to the tractive force.

questions.text: A wooden plank of cross-section 200 mm × 50 mm is used as a simply supported beam. Compared with laying it flat (50 mm vertical), placing it on edge (200 mm vertical) increases the load it can carry for the same allowable bending stress by a factor of
solution: Concept: Bending strength M = σZ, with section modulus Z = bd²/6 for a rectangle (d = depth in the plane of bending).
Exam tip: Strength ratio = d1/d2 (Z ∝ bd²), but the stiffness ratio is (d1/d2)² = 16 (I ∝ bd³). Do not mix them.

questions.text: A plane-stress element carries σ<sub>x</sub> = 60 MPa (tension), σ<sub>y</sub> = 20 MPa (compression) and τ<sub>xy</sub> = 30 MPa, as shown. The minimum principal stress, in MPa (with sign, tension positive), is ______
solution: Concept: σ1,2 = (σx + σy)/2 ± √[((σx − σy)/2)² + τxy²]; τmax = radius of Mohr's circle; tan 2θp = 2τxy/(σx − σy).
Take σ<sub>y</sub> = −20 MPa (compression is negative). Centre = (60 − 20)/2 = 20 MPa.
Radius = √(40² + 30²) = 50 MPa, so σ1 = 70 MPa and σ2 = 20 − 50 = −30 MPa; τmax = 50 MPa; θp = ½ tan⁻¹(60/80) = 18.4°.
Exam tip: The commonest error is entering the compressive stress as +20: that gives centre 40, radius 36.1 and a wrong σ2 of 3.9 MPa.

questions.text: A spring–mass–damper system has m = 5 kg, k = 20 kN/m and c = 250 N·s/m. Its damped natural frequency is
solution: Concept: ωn = √(k/m); cc = 2√(km) = 2mωn; ζ = c/cc; ωd = ωn√(1 − ζ²).
Exam tip: 52.4 rad/s is ωn√(1 − 2ζ²), the frequency of peak amplitude in forced vibration — a different formula. 9.25 is 58.1 rad/s converted to Hz.

questions.text: A beam of solid circular section, 100 mm in diameter, carries a shear force of 60 kN. The maximum shear stress in the section, in MPa, is ______
solution: Concept: τ = VAȳ/(Ib); its peak at the neutral axis is (4/3)τavg for a circle and (3/2)τavg for a rectangle.
Exam tip: Thin-walled tube: 2τavg; I-section: the web carries nearly all the shear, τmax ≈ V/(web area).

questions.text: In the simple gear train shown, gear A (20 teeth) drives gear C (40 teeth) through an idler B (50 teeth). If A turns at 400 rpm clockwise, gear C turns at
solution: Concept: In a simple train, Nlast/Nfirst = Tfirst/Tlast; idlers do not change the ratio, only the direction (each external mesh reverses rotation).
A (cw) → B (ccw) → C (cw): 200 rpm clockwise (B).
Exam tip: Odd number of idlers → same direction as the driver; even number → opposite. In a compound train the ratio is the product of driven/driver teeth for each pair.

questions.text: A slider moves outward along a straight rotating link with a constant velocity of 1.5 m/s relative to the link, while the link turns at a uniform 20 rad/s. The magnitude of the Coriolis component of the slider's acceleration, in m/s², is ______
solution: Concept: Coriolis component ac = 2vω, where v is the sliding velocity relative to the rotating link; it acts perpendicular to the link.
Direction: rotate the relative velocity vector by 90° in the sense of ω.
Exam tip: Do not drop the factor 2 (30 m/s² is a trap). The Coriolis term exists only when a point slides on a rotating link — never for a slider on a fixed guide.

questions.text: In a reciprocating engine the crank is 60 mm, the connecting rod is 240 mm and the reciprocating mass is 2 kg. The engine runs at 1500 rpm. The maximum secondary unbalanced force and its frequency are
opts: 2961 N, varying at the crank frequency
740 N, varying at the crank frequency
740 N, varying at twice the crank frequency
185 N, varying at twice the crank frequency
questions.ans: (C) 740 N, varying at twice the crank frequency
solution: Concept: Primary force = mω²r cosθ; secondary force = mω²r cos 2θ/n, where n = l/r; the secondary term varies at twice the crank speed.
Secondary maximum = 2961/4 = 740 N at twice the crank frequency (C).
Exam tip: Dividing by n² (185 N) is a common slip. Think of the secondary force as from an imaginary crank of length r/(4n) rotating at 2ω.

questions.text: A rotor with a mass moment of inertia of 10 kg·m² is fixed to the free end of a vertical steel shaft 1 m long and 50 mm in diameter, whose other end is rigidly clamped. Neglecting the inertia of the shaft and taking G = 80 GPa, the natural frequency of torsional vibration, in Hz, is ______
solution: Concept: Torsional stiffness kt = GJ/L, J = πd⁴/32; fn = (1/2π)√(kt/I).
Exam tip: The torsional formulas mirror linear ones: k → GJ/L, m → I. Including shaft inertia adds Ishaft/3 to the rotor.

questions.text: An M16 bolt is to be tightened to an initial preload of 20 kN. Taking the usual torque coefficient of 0.2, the required tightening torque is
solution: Concept: Tightening torque T = K Fi d, with torque (nut) factor K ≈ 0.2 for dry steel threads, d = nominal diameter.
Exam tip: Keep d in metres for N·m. A common design rule for preload is Fi ≈ 0.75 × proof load for reusable joints (0.9 for permanent).

questions.text: A 10 kg mass is supported as shown: spring k<sub>1</sub> = 6 kN/m hangs from the ceiling and carries a light rigid plate, from which the mass hangs on two springs k<sub>2</sub> = k<sub>3</sub> = 6 kN/m side by side. The natural frequency of vertical vibration, in Hz, is ______
solution: Concept: Springs in parallel: k = k1 + k2; in series: 1/k = 1/k1 + 1/k2; fn = (1/2π)√(k/m).
k<sub>2</sub> ∥ k<sub>3</sub> = 12 kN/m; in series with k<sub>1</sub>: k<sub>eq</sub> = (6 × 12)/(6 + 12) = 4 kN/m.
Exam tip: Springs that carry the same force are in series; springs that share the same deflection are in parallel. Gravity does not change fn of a linear spring–mass system.

questions.text: A V-belt runs in a pulley groove of included angle 40°. The angle of contact is 160° and μ = 0.25. The ratio of the tight-side to slack-side tension (ignoring centrifugal tension) is
solution: Concept: Flat belt: T1/T2 = eμθ. V-belt: T1/T2 = eμθ cosec β, where β is HALF the groove angle.
Exam tip: Using the full groove angle (sin 40°) gives 2.96; forgetting the wedge effect gives 2.01. With centrifugal tension use (T1 − Tc)/(T2 − Tc).

questions.text: A close-coiled helical spring has a mean coil diameter of 40 mm and a wire diameter of 5 mm. It carries an axial load of 300 N. Using Wahl's factor, the maximum shear stress in the wire, in MPa, is ______
solution: Concept: τ = K × 8PD/(πd³), with spring index C = D/d and Wahl factor K = (4C − 1)/(4C − 4) + 0.615/C.
Exam tip: Also remember k = Gd⁴/(8D³n) for stiffness. K corrects for both direct shear and curvature; the shear-stress factor alone is Ks = 1 + 0.5/C.
